Szydlow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Szydłów, Poland

Demolished. Szydłów's structured Jewish community existed from at least 1468, the same year King Kazimierz Jagiellończyk granted rights for this cemetery — one of the earliest such grants documented in this collection. By 1939, the community numbered about 1,500, most murdered by the Germans in 1942. The cemetery became a burial place for Holocaust victims, including those killed during the 1942 ghetto liquidation and further 1943 killings; a 1946 report found 1,141 'completely neglected' graves still present, with the site then used as pasture. Between 2017 and 2018, the Nissenbaum Family Foundation built a partial fence around the site.
